passages.heading: THE PEOPLE’S CHOICE.
passages.text: Rachel Rodriguez for Lieutenant Governor

passages.heading: THE PEOPLE’S CHOICE.
passages.text: Independent leadership committed to making Florida affordable, accountable, and centered on the people who call it home.

passages.heading: Florida Should Work for Floridians Again.
passages.text: Florida is growing, but too many of the people who built their lives here are being priced out, overlooked, or ignored.

passages.heading: Florida Should Work for Floridians Again.
passages.text: Families are confronting rising housing, insurance, grocery, utility, and everyday living costs. Teachers are undervalued. Seniors are worried about remaining in the communities they love. Young Floridians are questioning whether they can build a future here.

passages.heading: Florida Should Work for Floridians Again.
passages.text: Neither left nor right. Neither Republican nor Democrat. This is the People’s Party, and Russo Rodriguez is the People’s Choice.

passages.heading: Two Different Paths. One Shared Purpose.
passages.text: A complementary governing partnership combining executive leadership with legal accountability.

passages.heading: Frank J. Russo
passages.text: A Florida-born businessman, entrepreneur, insurance executive, developer, humanitarian, father, and faith-guided leader.

passages.heading: Rachel Rodriguez
passages.text: A Florida attorney, working mother, wife and mother of three, business builder, Cuban-American, and faith-guided advocate.

passages.heading: The People’s Choice
passages.text: Florida should be a place where people can build a life, raise a family, start a business and afford to stay. Neither left nor right. Neither Republican nor Democrat. This is the People’s Party, and Russo Rodriguez is the People’s Choice.

passages.heading: Make Florida Affordable Again
passages.text: Florida's success should be measured by whether the people who already live here can afford to stay here. Families don't experience insurance, housing, property taxes and everyday costs as separate problems - they all come out of the same paycheck.

passages.heading: Make Florida Affordable Again
passages.text: Frank's affordability agenda takes on those pressures together - with practical plans to lower costs, protect homeowners, expand opportunity and invest in the people who make Florida work.

passages.heading: Invest in the People Building Florida’s Future
passages.text: Great schools start with great teachers - and Frank believes the people making education policy should listen to the people actually living it.

passages.heading: Invest in the People Building Florida’s Future
passages.text: Frank wants to raise Florida's average teacher salary to at least $75,000, strengthen teacher recruitment and retention, and expand skilled trades, apprenticeships and career pathways so every student has a path to a good-paying future. He is also working to become a Florida substitute teacher because leadership begins by listening - and Frank believes elected officials should experience the classrooms their decisions affect.

passages.heading: Build Florida’s Next Economy
passages.text: Frank wants Florida to lead the next generation of American innovation - attracting new technology, investment and jobs while making sure Floridians have the opportunity to share in that growth.

passages.heading: Build Florida’s Next Economy
passages.text: His approach is pro-innovation, pro-business and pro-accountability - protecting taxpayers and communities, preparing Florida workers for an economy transformed by AI, and giving more entrepreneurs a fair shot to build something successful.

passages.heading: Secure. Legal. Humane.
passages.text: Frank believes Florida can protect its communities, uphold the rule of law, support legal immigration and still treat people with dignity. Those principles are not in conflict.

passages.heading: Secure. Legal. Humane.
passages.text: His Common Sense Immigration Principles focus on stronger public safety partnerships, targeting violent criminals, traffickers and gangs, cracking down on worker exploitation, supporting legal immigration and pushing Washington to finally address a broken federal immigration system.

passages.heading: Your Health. Your Choice.
passages.text: Frank believes lawful medical decisions should be made by Floridians in consultation with their healthcare providers - not dictated by government.

passages.heading: Your Health. Your Choice.
passages.text: His Florida Medical Freedom Initiative protects informed consent and individual medical choice while strengthening patient rights, access to accurate information and transparency and accountability in public health decision-making.

passages.heading: Caring Capitalism
passages.text: Frank doesn't believe capitalism and compassion are opposites.

passages.heading: Caring Capitalism
passages.text: His philosophy is Caring Capitalism - encouraging entrepreneurship, investment, growth and extraordinary success while recognizing that a strong economy also depends on teachers, nurses, tradespeople, first responders, workers and families being able to afford a future here.

passages.heading: Caring Capitalism
passages.text: Humanity Over the Dollar doesn't mean rejecting success. It means making sure success strengthens Florida.

passages.heading: A movement prepared to listen, build, and serve.
passages.text: Hear Frank J. Russo share why he is running for Governor and why Russo–Rodriguez is the People’s Choice for the future of our state.

passages.heading: Join the People’s Party Movement.
passages.text: Share your contact information and interests so the campaign can keep you connected to opportunities to participate.

passages.heading: Join the People’s Party Movement.
passages.text: There is a place for you in this movement

passages.heading: This Is Our Florida. Let’s Build Its Future Together.
passages.text: Join Frank Russo and Rachel Rodriguez in the people-powered People’s Party movement and make Russo–Rodriguez the People’s Choice.

passages.heading: Make Florida Affordable Again
passages.text: Florida 9.9 - Invest in Florida's future through a proposed 9.9% consumption tax only on spending above $1 million, with the first $1 million exempt and the resulting revenue protected in public trust for housing, teachers, healthcare, skilled trades and the future of work. This replaces other taxes that currently take money while it’s being made; Frank’s plan harnesses money only when it is spent.

passages.heading: Make Florida Affordable Again
passages.text: Property Insurance Reform - Put homeowners first with a more affordable, accountable and transparent insurance system - backed by Frank's more than 30 years of experience in the industry.

passages.heading: Make Florida Affordable Again
passages.text: Housing Affordability & Accountability - Build more housing working Floridians can afford while demanding measurable results when taxpayer dollars and public incentives are involved.

passages.heading: Make Florida Affordable Again
passages.text: Property Tax Relief - Help Floridians keep more of what they earn, pursue additional relief for homeowners and hold government accountable for how property tax dollars are spent.

passages.heading: Build Florida’s Next Economy
passages.text: Data Centers & AI Infrastructure - Welcome technology investment while requiring major projects receiving public incentives to plan responsibly for power, water and infrastructure needs and deliver measurable benefits to the communities where they build.

passages.heading: Build Florida’s Next Economy
passages.text: AI & the Future of Work - Bring the jobs of the future to Florida while making sure Florida students and workers have the skills, training and opportunities to fill them.

passages.heading: Build Florida’s Next Economy
passages.text: Women’s Entrepreneurship - Give more women the tools to learn, launch and grow Florida businesses through practical training, professional support, access to capital and performance-based startup assistance.

passages.heading: Your Health. Your Choice.
passages.text: Leadership begins by listening. If there's an issue affecting your family, your business or your community that you believe Florida's next governor needs to address, Frank wants to hear it.

passages.heading: Make Florida Affordable for the People Who Live Here
passages.text: Florida is growing. Businesses are coming here. People are moving here. But Frank believes there is a simple question we need to ask: Can the people who already live here afford to stay? Families don't experience insurance, property taxes, rent, electricity, groceries and everyday expenses as separate issues. They all come out of the same paycheck. If we're going to say Florida is succeeding, that success has to show up in the lives of the people who call Florida home. Frank's affordability agenda is about practical solutions, accountability and measurable results - not creating more government for the sake of creating government.

passages.heading: Property Insurance Reform
passages.text: Florida homeowners should not have to wonder whether the next insurance renewal will make their home unaffordable.

passages.heading: Property Insurance Reform
passages.text: With more than 30 years in the insurance industry, Frank understands this system from the inside. His plan is focused on bringing greater accountability, competition and stability to Florida's insurance market - and making sure homeowners come first.

passages.heading: Property Tax Relief
passages.text: You shouldn't be taxed out of a home you've worked your entire life to own.

passages.heading: Property Tax Relief
passages.text: Frank supports responsible property tax relief while protecting schools, public safety and essential services. But he also believes government needs to do its part - eliminate waste, spend smarter and show taxpayers where their money is going.

passages.heading: Housing Accountability & Rent Relief
passages.text: Florida needs more housing that working people can actually afford.

passages.heading: Housing Accountability & Rent Relief
passages.text: Frank wants to work with developers and the private sector to build more housing - but when taxpayer dollars or public incentives are involved, taxpayers deserve to know what they're getting in return. His plan ties public support to real, measurable and lasting affordability.

passages.heading: Florida 9.9 - Invest in Florida’s Future
passages.text: Frank believes in capitalism. He believes in entrepreneurship, building businesses, creating jobs and becoming extraordinarily successful.

passages.heading: Florida 9.9 - Invest in Florida’s Future
passages.text: He also believes extraordinary success comes with an opportunity to help keep Florida affordable for the people who teach our children, care for our families, build our homes and keep this state running. Ensuring local and state essential services for all Floridians also should not burden Floridian families (like property tax) in such a way that they are unable to build wealth for their children’s future. Frank's Florida 9.9 proposal would apply a 9.9% consumption state tax only to spending above $1 million. The first $1 million in spending would not be taxed, and implementation of this plan would require the approval from Florida voters through their elected representatives.

passages.heading: Florida 9.9 - Invest in Florida’s Future
passages.text: The revenue from this plan would be protected in public trust, not in government agency hands and reinvested in priorities including housing, teachers, healthcare workers, skilled trades and preparing Florida's workforce for AI and automation - with independent audits, public reporting and protections against politicians diverting the money elsewhere.

passages.heading: The Test Is Simple
passages.text: Frank believes every affordability proposal should have to answer one question:

passages.heading: The Test Is Simple
passages.text: Does this make it easier for Floridians to afford to build a life here?

passages.heading: The Test Is Simple
passages.text: If the answer is no, we need to do better.

passages.heading: Invest in the People Building Florida’s Future
passages.text: Florida's future starts in its classrooms. Frank Russo believes we cannot say children are our future while undervaluing the people responsible for educating them. And we cannot prepare young Floridians for a changing economy if we continue pretending a four-year college degree is the only path to success. Frank's plan starts with a simple idea: invest in children, respect teachers and give every student a real path to a good-paying future.

passages.heading: Treat Teachers Like the Professionals They Are
passages.text: Florida should be competing for the best teachers in America - not losing talented educators because they can't afford to build a life here.

passages.heading: Treat Teachers Like the Professionals They Are
passages.text: Frank is proposing to raise Florida's average teacher salary to at least $75,000 a year while strengthening teacher recruitment, retention and classroom support.

passages.heading: Treat Teachers Like the Professionals They Are
passages.text: Teachers need to know that Florida respects their profession, listens to their experiences and understands what they're being asked to do every day.

passages.heading: Treat Teachers Like the Professionals They Are
passages.text: We should cut bureaucracy before we cut teachers.

passages.heading: Leadership Begins by Listening
passages.text: Frank doesn't believe politicians should make decisions about classrooms they've never spent time in.

passages.heading: Leadership Begins by Listening
passages.text: That's why he began the process of becoming a Florida substitute teacher - including completing the fingerprinting process - so he can experience today's classrooms firsthand and better understand what teachers and students are actually facing.

passages.heading: Leadership Begins by Listening
passages.text: His challenge to other elected leaders is simple:

passages.heading: Leadership Begins by Listening
passages.text: Spend time in a classroom. Talk to teachers. Listen to students and parents. Understand the reality before writing the policy.

passages.heading: Leadership Begins by Listening
passages.text: Frank believes leadership begins by listening - and education policy should be no different.

passages.heading: Put More Money Into Classrooms - Not Bureaucracy
passages.text: Frank believes raising teacher pay has to be accompanied by a serious look at where Florida's education dollars are going.

passages.heading: Put More Money Into Classrooms - Not Bureaucracy
passages.text: His approach is to reduce administrative waste and redirect resources toward teachers and classrooms rather than allowing bureaucracy to continue growing. His existing education proposal also calls for using state reserves as a bridge for increased teacher compensation rather than initially funding the increase through new taxes.

passages.heading: Put More Money Into Classrooms - Not Bureaucracy
passages.text: Put the people teaching our children ahead of the bureaucracy surrounding them.

passages.heading: Build Confidence, Character & Capability
passages.text: Education should prepare children to pass tests - but Frank doesn't believe test scores alone define a successful education.

passages.heading: Build Confidence, Character & Capability
passages.text: He wants Florida schools to help young people develop confidence, character and capability so they're prepared to make decisions, solve problems, adapt and succeed when they leave the classroom.

passages.heading: Build Confidence, Character & Capability
passages.text: For Frank, education isn't only about what a child knows.

passages.heading: Build Confidence, Character & Capability
passages.text: It's also about whether that child believes they can build something with what they've learned.

passages.heading: Bring the Skilled Trades Back
passages.text: Not every successful career begins with a four-year college degree.

passages.heading: Bring the Skilled Trades Back
passages.text: Florida needs electricians, plumbers, HVAC technicians, construction professionals and skilled workers - and those careers can provide young Floridians with good-paying opportunities without requiring them to take on four years of college debt.

passages.heading: Bring the Skilled Trades Back
passages.text: Frank wants to bring skilled-trades education back into Florida high schools so more students can graduate with certifications, practical skills and a direct path into the workforce.

passages.heading: Earn While You Learn
passages.text: Frank's plan would expand technical training and create more paid apprenticeship opportunities connecting students directly with employers and skilled careers.

passages.heading: Earn While You Learn
passages.text: He also wants experienced tradesmen and tradeswomen to have greater opportunities to teach the next generation - recognizing that decades of real-world experience can be just as valuable in a technical classroom as a traditional academic credential.

passages.heading: Earn While You Learn
passages.text: Students should be able to leave high school with more than a diploma.

passages.heading: Earn While You Learn
passages.text: College. A trade. An apprenticeship. Entrepreneurship. A career.

passages.heading: Earn While You Learn
passages.text: The goal is opportunity - not forcing every young Floridian down the same path.

passages.heading: Prepare Floridians for the AI Economy
passages.text: Artificial intelligence is going to change what work looks like.

passages.heading: Prepare Floridians for the AI Economy
passages.text: Frank believes Florida should prepare for that change rather than wait until workers are displaced by it.

passages.heading: Prepare Floridians for the AI Economy
passages.text: That means strengthening skilled careers that are difficult to automate while also preparing students and workers to participate in AI and emerging industries.

passages.heading: Prepare Floridians for the AI Economy
passages.text: Frank's Florida 9.9 proposal would reinforce that investment through the protected Florida Future Fund - supporting teacher pay, skilled trades and apprenticeships, and education and retraining for workers affected by AI and automation.

passages.heading: The Test Is Simple
passages.text: Frank doesn't believe the success of Florida's education system should be measured only by another ranking or report from Tallahassee.

passages.heading: The Test Is Simple
passages.text: Are we attracting and keeping great teachers?

passages.heading: The Test Is Simple
passages.text: Are our children prepared for life after graduation?

passages.heading: The Test Is Simple
passages.text: Does every student have a path to a good-paying future?

passages.heading: The Test Is Simple
passages.text: If we can answer yes, Florida is moving in the right direction.

passages.heading: Build Florida’s Next Economy
passages.text: Florida should be one of the best places in America to build a company, develop new technology, create jobs and turn a good idea into something successful. Frank wants Florida leading the next generation of American innovation - but growth should work for the people who already live here. That means welcoming investment while protecting taxpayers and communities, preparing Floridians for an economy being transformed by AI, and giving more entrepreneurs the opportunity to build and grow businesses here. Frank's approach is simple: Welcome innovation. Create opportunity. Demand accountability.

passages.heading: Data Centers & AI Infrastructure
passages.text: Florida should compete for AI, technology investment and high-paying jobs - but existing residents shouldn't be left paying for the infrastructure that makes major developments possible.

passages.heading: Data Centers & AI Infrastructure
passages.text: Frank's Florida Community Dividend framework would require major data center projects receiving public incentives to plan responsibly for their power, water and infrastructure needs while providing binding, measurable benefits to the communities where they build.

passages.heading: AI & the Future of Work
passages.text: AI is going to change how Floridians work, what skills employers need and which industries grow.

passages.heading: AI & the Future of Work
passages.text: Frank wants Florida preparing now - attracting the industries and jobs of the future while investing in education, skilled workforce programs and opportunities that help Floridians adapt as AI and automation reshape the economy. His Florida Future Fund specifically includes investment in preparing students and workers for AI and emerging technologies.

passages.heading: Women’s Entrepreneurship
passages.text: A good idea shouldn't depend on having the right connections or already having access to capital.

passages.heading: Women’s Entrepreneurship
passages.text: Frank's proposed $100 million Florida Women's Entrepreneur Initiative would help qualified women learn the fundamentals of running a business, develop a viable plan, access professional support, compete for performance-based startup assistance and grow businesses that create Florida jobs.

passages.heading: Innovation That Works for Florida
passages.text: Frank doesn't believe innovation should be measured simply by how many companies move here, how many projects get announced or how much government spends.

passages.heading: Innovation That Works for Florida
passages.text: Are we creating Florida jobs? Are Floridians prepared for the future? Are taxpayers getting measurable results? And are more people getting a fair shot at building something successful?

passages.heading: Innovation That Works for Florida
passages.text: That's how Florida can lead the future without leaving Floridians behind.

passages.heading: Secure. Legal. Humane.
passages.text: Frank believes in secure borders. He believes in the rule of law. And as Governor, his first responsibility will always be keeping Floridians safe. But immigration is personal to Frank too. His family came to this country for the same reason generations of families have come here - for a chance to work hard, build a life and give their children something better. That's why Frank doesn't believe we have to choose between enforcing the law and treating people with dignity. Protect our communities. Follow the law. Support legal immigration. Treat people like human beings. We can do all four.

passages.heading: Keep Floridians Safe
passages.text: Frank's first responsibility as Governor is to keep Floridians safe.

passages.heading: Keep Floridians Safe
passages.text: That means focusing law enforcement resources on the people who actually threaten our communities - violent criminals, drug traffickers, human traffickers and transnational gangs.

passages.heading: Keep Floridians Safe
passages.text: As Governor, Frank would strengthen partnerships between Florida law enforcement and federal agencies and prioritize state resources toward removing people who commit violent crimes and pose genuine threats to public safety.

passages.heading: Keep Floridians Safe
passages.text: If you are a violent criminal, a trafficker or you're here to hurt people, we need to deal with that. There should be no question about it.

passages.heading: Secure the Border - And Be Honest About Who Controls It
passages.text: Frank supports securing America's border.

passages.heading: Secure the Border - And Be Honest About Who Controls It
passages.text: But he's also not going to pretend the Governor of Florida controls the United States border.

passages.heading: Secure the Border - And Be Honest About Who Controls It
passages.text: Washington does. And Washington needs to do its job.

passages.heading: Secure the Border - And Be Honest About Who Controls It
passages.text: Immigration is primarily a federal responsibility. A Florida governor cannot create citizenship, establish federal immigration status or single-handedly fix the nation's immigration system.

passages.heading: Secure the Border - And Be Honest About Who Controls It
passages.text: What Florida can do is strengthen public safety partnerships, combat trafficking and exploitation, enforce the laws within its authority and make sure our state is doing its part.

passages.heading: Secure the Border - And Be Honest About Who Controls It
passages.text: Frank believes leadership starts with being honest about what you can control - and then getting to work on it.

passages.heading: Go After the People Exploiting Workers
passages.text: Frank believes accountability has to go both ways.

passages.heading: Go After the People Exploiting Workers
passages.text: If a business or individual knowingly exploits undocumented workers or commits immigration-related fraud, they should be held accountable too.

passages.heading: Go After the People Exploiting Workers
passages.text: Frank would crack down on that exploitation while strengthening employment verification requirements for state agencies and state contractors so taxpayer-funded jobs comply with federal law.

passages.heading: Go After the People Exploiting Workers
passages.text: If you're breaking the law to exploit vulnerable workers, you don't get a free pass either.

passages.heading: Respect People Who Follow the Rules
passages.text: Frank believes legal immigration has helped build America.

passages.heading: Respect People Who Follow the Rules
passages.text: People who come here legally, work hard, follow the rules, raise families, build businesses and contribute to their communities should know that matters.

passages.heading: Respect People Who Follow the Rules
passages.text: Frank would expand English-language and workforce-development opportunities that help legal immigrants successfully integrate into Florida's economy.

passages.heading: Respect People Who Follow the Rules
passages.text: For Frank, this comes back to his own family's story.

passages.heading: Respect People Who Follow the Rules
passages.text: His family came to America looking for an opportunity to work hard and build something better for the next generation.

passages.heading: Respect People Who Follow the Rules
passages.text: That's part of Frank's story. And it's part of America's story.

passages.heading: Washington Needs to Fix What’s Broken
passages.text: For too long, Washington has argued about immigration without fixing the system.

passages.heading: Washington Needs to Fix What’s Broken
passages.text: Frank believes the federal government needs to secure the border, enforce the law and finally create a legal process that actually works.

passages.heading: Washington Needs to Fix What’s Broken
passages.text: He supports calling on Congress to establish an earned federal process for long-term, law-abiding residents who meet strict legal requirements, including background checks and compliance with federal law.

passages.heading: Washington Needs to Fix What’s Broken
passages.text: This isn't something Frank can create as Governor - and he won't pretend otherwise.

passages.heading: Washington Needs to Fix What’s Broken
passages.text: But he can use Florida's voice to push Washington to act.

passages.heading: Washington Needs to Fix What’s Broken
passages.text: Frank believes the principle should be clear:

passages.heading: Washington Needs to Fix What’s Broken
passages.text: People who commit violent crimes should be removed. People who work hard, obey the law and contribute to their communities deserve a system that is fair, orderly and rooted in the rule of law.

passages.heading: Get the Right People at the Table
passages.text: Frank doesn't believe Tallahassee has all the answers.

passages.heading: Get the Right People at the Table
passages.text: He would establish a Governor's Immigration Advisory Council bringing together law enforcement, business leaders, agriculture, faith leaders, legal immigrants and local officials.

passages.heading: Get the Right People at the Table
passages.text: These are people who see different sides of immigration every day.

passages.heading: Get the Right People at the Table
passages.text: What's working? What's not? What are we missing? And what can Florida actually do better?

passages.heading: The Ellis Island Promise
passages.text: Frank calls his approach The Ellis Island Promise because America should never have to choose between strength and humanity.

passages.heading: The Ellis Island Promise
passages.text: Frank believes America has always been strongest when we combine accountability with opportunity.

passages.heading: The Ellis Island Promise
passages.text: The Ellis Island Promise is about keeping both.

passages.heading: The Test Is Simple
passages.text: Immigration has become one of the most divisive issues in America. Frank doesn't believe shouting louder is going to fix it.

passages.heading: The Test Is Simple
passages.text: Are we enforcing the law fairly and responsibly?

passages.heading: The Test Is Simple
passages.text: Are we respecting people who follow the legal process?

passages.heading: The Test Is Simple
passages.text: Are we holding criminals, traffickers and people who exploit workers accountable?

passages.heading: The Test Is Simple
passages.text: And are we still treating people like human beings?

passages.heading: The Test Is Simple
passages.text: Frank believes we don't have to choose between strength and humanity.

passages.heading: The Test Is Simple
passages.text: We can be strong and still be decent. We can do both.

passages.heading: Your Health. Your Choice.
passages.text: Frank believes lawful medical decisions should be made by Floridians in consultation with their healthcare providers - not dictated by government. Government has a role. It should protect public health, make accurate information available, establish fair laws and be transparent about the decisions it makes. But Frank doesn't believe government should substitute its judgment for yours. Your health. Your family. Your choice - with good information, personal responsibility and the freedom to make an informed decision.

passages.heading: Protect Informed Consent
passages.text: Medical freedom starts with knowing what you're agreeing to.

passages.heading: Protect Informed Consent
passages.text: Frank believes Floridians should have access to accurate, understandable information before making lawful medical decisions.

passages.heading: Protect Informed Consent
passages.text: Patients should be able to ask questions, understand the risks and benefits of their options and make decisions in consultation with healthcare professionals they trust.

passages.heading: Protect Informed Consent
passages.text: Give people the facts. Let them ask questions. Respect their right to make an informed decision.

passages.heading: Strengthen Patient Rights
passages.text: Patients shouldn't feel like bystanders in decisions about their own health.

passages.heading: Strengthen Patient Rights
passages.text: Frank wants to strengthen access to medical records, treatment information and shared decision-making between patients and their healthcare providers.

passages.heading: Strengthen Patient Rights
passages.text: That means giving Floridians the information they need to participate meaningfully in decisions about their care.

passages.heading: Strengthen Patient Rights
passages.text: The patient should be part of the conversation - not the last person brought into it.

passages.heading: Give Floridians the Facts
passages.text: Frank believes public health agencies have an obligation to be clear with the public.

passages.heading: Give Floridians the Facts
passages.text: When government makes a major public health recommendation, Floridians should be able to understand the scientific evidence and reasoning behind it.

passages.heading: Give Floridians the Facts
passages.text: Frank's initiative would increase transparency in public health communications and expand access to clear, evidence-based health information so families can make informed decisions for themselves.

passages.heading: Give Floridians the Facts
passages.text: Frank doesn't believe transparency weakens public trust.

passages.heading: Freedom Comes With Responsibility
passages.text: Frank believes medical freedom and personal responsibility go together.

passages.heading: Freedom Comes With Responsibility
passages.text: People should have the freedom to make lawful decisions about their health - and government should encourage Floridians to take an active role in protecting it.

passages.heading: Freedom Comes With Responsibility
passages.text: That includes preventive care, healthy lifestyles and informed healthcare choices rather than relying on one-size-fits-all mandates.

passages.heading: Freedom Comes With Responsibility
passages.text: For Frank, freedom doesn't mean ignoring responsibility.

passages.heading: Freedom Comes With Responsibility
passages.text: Freedom and responsibility go hand in hand.

passages.heading: Make Public Health Decisions More Transparent
passages.text: Frank believes government should be held to the same standard of accountability it expects from everyone else.

passages.heading: Make Public Health Decisions More Transparent
passages.text: When major public health decisions are made, Floridians deserve to know:

passages.heading: Make Public Health Decisions More Transparent
passages.text: Frank's initiative would give Floridians greater visibility into how major healthcare and public health policies are developed and how decisions affecting them are made.

passages.heading: Respect the Voters
passages.text: Frank believes the same principle applies when Floridians are asked to make major healthcare or public-policy decisions themselves.

passages.heading: Respect the Voters
passages.text: That includes issues such as Florida's ongoing debate over adult-use cannabis.

passages.heading: Respect the Voters
passages.text: Frank believes voters ultimately decide constitutional amendments. His responsibility is to make sure Floridians receive clear ballot language, accurate public education and honest information so they understand what they're being asked to decide.

passages.heading: Respect the Voters
passages.text: Whether the question involves healthcare, public health or cannabis policy, Frank's position is consistent:

passages.heading: Respect the Voters
passages.text: Give people the facts. Be honest about the choices. Trust Floridians to make an informed decision.

passages.heading: Government Serves the People
passages.text: Frank's Medical Freedom Initiative is ultimately about a broader principle that guides how he believes government should operate.

passages.heading: Government Serves the People
passages.text: Government serves the people - not the other way around.

passages.heading: Government Serves the People
passages.text: Frank doesn't believe a Governor's job is to substitute his judgment for yours.

passages.heading: Government Serves the People
passages.text: His job is to protect your rights, make government transparent, provide Floridians with accurate information and build public trust through honesty and accountability.

passages.heading: The Test Is Simple
passages.text: When government makes decisions involving the health and medical freedom of Floridians, Frank believes we should ask:

passages.heading: The Test Is Simple
passages.text: Is government being transparent about the evidence and reasoning behind its decisions?

passages.heading: The Test Is Simple
passages.text: And are we respecting the right of Floridians to make lawful choices for themselves and their families?

passages.heading: The Test Is Simple
passages.text: Frank believes individual liberty and accountability aren't opposites.

passages.heading: The Test Is Simple
passages.text: Protect people's rights. Give them the facts. Trust them to make informed decisions.

passages.heading: Invest in Florida’s Future
passages.text: Frank Russo is a capitalist. He wants Florida to be one of the best places in America to start a company, build a legacy for one’s children, invest, create jobs and become extraordinarily successful. But Frank is also a caring capitalist. He believes “to whom much is given, much is required:” extraordinary success and responsibility coexist - and that Florida can remain pro-business and pro-growth while making a greater investment in the teachers, nurses, skilled workers, young people and families who will determine our state's future.

passages.heading: What Does 9.9 Mean?
passages.text: The first $1 million in spending - $0 in proposed Florida consumption tax.

passages.heading: What Does 9.9 Mean?
passages.text: Spending costs above $1 million - proposed 9.9% consumption tax.

passages.heading: What Does 9.9 Mean?
passages.text: The tax can replace other taxes that take money Floridians are trying to make or build from investment, like certain business and sales taxes.

passages.heading: Where Would the Money Go?
passages.text: Frank does not want this money disappearing into Tallahassee's general fund.

passages.heading: Where Would the Money Go?
passages.text: Revenue would be legally protected and dedicated to investments in Floridians and Florida's economic future.

passages.heading: Where Would the Money Go?
passages.text: Teachers - Raise Florida's average teacher salary to at least $75,000 and improve recruitment and retention.

passages.heading: Where Would the Money Go?
passages.text: Housing - Expand first-time homeownership opportunities and address housing affordability.

passages.heading: Where Would the Money Go?
passages.text: Healthcare - Address nursing shortages and strengthen Florida's healthcare workforce.

passages.heading: Where Would the Money Go?
passages.text: Skilled Trades - Expand trade schools, apprenticeships and skilled workforce programs.

passages.heading: Where Would the Money Go?
passages.text: AI & the Future of Work - Prepare students and workers for emerging technologies and help Floridians adapt as automation changes industries and jobs.

passages.heading: Not Another Blank Check for Tallahassee
passages.text: Frank believes one of the first questions Floridians should ask is:

passages.heading: Not Another Blank Check for Tallahassee
passages.text: Why should we give government more money?

passages.heading: Not Another Blank Check for Tallahassee
passages.text: His answer isn't that Floridians should trust government more.

passages.heading: Not Another Blank Check for Tallahassee
passages.text: It's that government should have to prove where the money went.

passages.heading: Not Another Blank Check for Tallahassee
passages.text: Dedicated use - Money could only be spent on purposes established in law.

passages.heading: Not Another Blank Check for Tallahassee
passages.text: Independent audits - Recurring financial and performance audits.

passages.heading: Not Another Blank Check for Tallahassee
passages.text: Public transparency - Floridians could see where the money goes and what results it produces.

passages.heading: Not Another Blank Check for Tallahassee
passages.text: Conflict-of-interest protections - Guardrails against favoritism involving friends, family, donors or insiders.

passages.heading: Not Another Blank Check for Tallahassee
passages.text: Competitive procurement - Objective processes for contracts and grants.

passages.heading: Not Another Blank Check for Tallahassee
passages.text: Anti-diversion protections - Dedicated money couldn't simply be swept into unrelated spending.

passages.heading: Not Another Blank Check for Tallahassee
passages.text: Enforcement - Misuse could result in repayment, clawbacks or other consequences.

passages.heading: Not Another Blank Check for Tallahassee
passages.text: The rules should apply to everyone - including Frank.

passages.heading: Protect Small Businesses and Job Creation
passages.text: Frank does not want the proposal to unintentionally punish legitimate business activity, entrepreneurship or investment.

passages.heading: Protect Small Businesses and Job Creation
passages.text: Detailed legislation would include protections for legitimate pass-through business operations, investment and job creation, with additional fiscal modeling, legal review and implementation details developed before the proposal moves forward.

passages.heading: Protect Small Businesses and Job Creation
passages.text: Success is welcome in Florida. Wealth is welcome in Florida. Entrepreneurship is welcome in Florida.

passages.heading: Protect Small Businesses and Job Creation
passages.text: This proposal isn't about having fewer successful people here. Frank wants more.

passages.heading: Protect Small Businesses and Job Creation
passages.text: It's about asking whether Florida can remain one of America's best places to create wealth while also investing in the people and workforce that make that prosperity possible.

passages.heading: The Test Is Simple
passages.text: Frank believes Floridians should be able to answer three questions:

passages.heading: The Test Is Simple
passages.text: Can Floridians see exactly where the money goes?

passages.heading: The Test Is Simple
passages.text: If we can't answer yes, the policy isn't finished.
